judged_text: The rewritten `.update` context contains only the automatic-group test, so no test in this diff exercises the non-automatic success path of the rewritten update action — `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i` (controller lines 38), `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` (line 39) and `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` (line 41) — even though the diff changed the wire format from params[:group][:name] to flat params[:name] and deleted the old test that verified rename (`group.name.should == 'fred'`). A regression in the new flat-param reading (e.g., reverting to params[:group][:name] or a typo'd alias_level key) makes every admin rename/alias-level edit a silent no-op — the server returns success_json, nothing persists — and the suite stays green because the only .update test hits group 1 (automatic), where the name assignment is skipped by design; I checked the only test file in the diff (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb) and its final .update context has exactly one test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites Admin::GroupsController#update to read flat params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) instead of `params[:group][...]`, and also changes the client model to send `data: this.asJSON()` (no `group:` wrapper). In the updated spec, the `.update` context now contains only one test and it targets an automatic group (`id: 1`), where `group.name = params[:name]` is intentionally skipped. The old non-automatic rename/member update coverage (e.g., expecting `group.name == 'fred'`) was removed, and no new test asserts that a non-automatic group persists `name`, `visible`, or `alias_level` via the new flat-param format. This is a concrete coverage gap for the rewritten update path, not a proven runtime bug in the diff itself.
